_README: This file is managed by LazyCue (see shelley/lazycue). Do NOT edit by hand — it is the cached, machine-generated DSL for a self-healing browser test. To change behavior, edit the test description and re-run LazyCue.
description: A built-in profile is restored only after confirmation, without changing a live conversation's settings. The built-in profile "Default" has been customized (it now differs from its built-in settings, voice prompt included), a profile "E2E restore" exists, and the conversation /c/{{SLUG}} uses "Default". Call "Default" returns "edited" while the stored Default profile is the customized one, "built-in" once it equals the built-in one again (otherwise its JSON); call "default profile" returns "unchanged" while the default profile is the one it was at the start; call "conversation settings" returns "unchanged" while the conversation's settings are what they were at the start; call "restore answer" returns "ok" once the server answered the page's restore of Default with success ("none" before one, otherwise the status). The screen is a 1280x800 desktop window. Name elements by ARIA role and accessible name, as Playwright's getByRole does; "named X" means an exact name match, "whose name contains X" a substring one. "The panel" is ".model-picker-panel". To "open the knob": click ".model-picker-inline .p-select-label"; the panel should be visible. To "edit tools": click the button whose name contains "Edit" inside the panel's data-testid "model-picker-tools"; the panel should be hidden. "The pills" are data-testid "model-picker-profiles"; "the profile X" is the radio (role "radio") named X inside them. To "edit profiles": click the button whose name contains "Edit" inside the pills. "The section" is data-testid "model-picker-auto-compaction"; "the section's X" is the radio named X inside it, and "the nudge" is its select (role "combobox"). "The dialog" is the element with role "dialog". "The X tool" is the dialog's radiogroup with aria-label X ('[role=radiogroup][aria-label="X"]'). "The auto compaction row" is the dialog's data-testid "auto-compaction". To "apply": click the dialog's button whose name contains "Apply to this conversation"; the dialog should be hidden. "The markers" are the data-testid "message-modelchange" elements. "Changed" is the panel's data-testid "model-picker-profile-changed". To "save as new" a name N: click changed's button whose name contains "Save as new…", fill changed's textbox named "New profile name" with N and press Enter in it. A "row" X is the dialog's data-testid "profile-row" containing the text X. "The row" is the dialog's data-testid "profile-row" whose ".profiles-item-name" has exactly the text "Default"; "restore" is its button named "Restore defaults", and "confirm" its button named "Restore “Default”". To "open the profiles": open the knob, then edit profiles. Perform the steps in order. 1. Navigate to /c/{{SLUG}} and open the profiles. 2. The row "E2E restore" must have no button whose name contains "Restore defaults" (count 0). 3. Restore should be enabled; click it. The row should contain the text "voice prompt". Call "Default": it must return "edited". 4. Click the row's button named "Cancel": there should be no confirm (count 0). 5. Click restore again, then the dialog's button whose name contains "Close modal". Open the profiles again: there should be no confirm (count 0). 6. Click restore, then confirm. Call "restore answer" until it returns "ok". Restore should be disabled. 7. Call "Default": it must return "built-in"; call "default profile": "unchanged"; call "conversation settings": "unchanged". 8. Click the dialog's button whose name contains "Close modal" and open the knob: changed should contain the text "Differs from Default".
